resources.string: Settings the phone needs for calls to be recorded.

ABP Call checks each setting it can read. Where the phone does not tell, tap the item to open the right screen, change it, and come back and tap Done. You can continue without finishing, but calls may then be missed.

Settings > About phone > tap the OS version (Build number) 7 times to unlock Developer options. Then Developer options (on Xiaomi: Additional settings > Developer options) > turn on USB debugging. It keeps recording working without Wi-Fi.

Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO: Additional settings > Developer options > turn on \"USB debugging (Security settings)\". It is separate from USB debugging and needs a SIM card and a signed-in Mi account. Without it the phone refuses ABP Call the permissions it needs.

Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO: Security app > Permissions > Autostart (on HyperOS also Settings > Apps > ABP Call > Autostart) > allow ABP Call. Without it the phone does not let ABP Call start again after a reboot or after it is cleared from memory. The phone does not tell apps this setting, so tap \"I did it\" when it is on.
ABP Call turns Wireless debugging back on if it is switched off, so calls keep being recorded. Also in Settings > Connection.
App info > Battery (on Xiaomi: Battery saver) > No restrictions. Otherwise the phone stops ABP Call in the background and calls are not recorded.

A system update can switch the debugging settings off and restart the phone at night. Xiaomi: Settings > About phone > HyperOS version > menu > Settings > turn off automatic download and install. Other phones: Developer options > Automatic system updates, off; Samsung: Software update > Auto download over Wi-Fi, off. The phone does not tell apps this setting, so tap \"I did it\" when it is off.
